full_judgment: 14. It appears that sale deed dated 3-2-59 was adduced in original by the plaintiff and on 19-9-90 admitted as exhibit No.1. The deed was produced from the custody of the plaintiff and such custody must be held to be proper as he was the purchaser. Under section 90 of the Evidence Act, the trial Court was obliged to presume that the signature and every part of the deed are of the persons purported to have signed and written, and was duly executed and attested. Such presumption is however rebuttable. Sharijan Nessa stated in her written statement in Title Suit No. 625 of 1975, exhibit 10, that Sonabi Nessa transferred her share to Sharijan Nessa. In the deed, it is recited that the land was owned and possessed by the vendors i.e. the petitioner and his mother Sonabi Nessa and there is no statement that they inherited any share from Tusta Pramanik. The petitioner has not yet challenged the deed before any appropriate forum. In the suit for specific performance of an agreement, no issue was rightly raised whether the deed is genuine and acted upon or not. In the frame of the suit, such an issue cannot be decided. But the trial Court appears to have converted the suit for specific performance into a suit for determination of title and decided that a thirty years old registered 'Kabala' exhibit 1 was forged and that Sharijan Nessa did not acquire any title by that 'Kabala'. The trial Court has no such jurisdiction to convert the suit into a suit for determination of title as was ruled by the Appellate Division in the case of Golam Kader vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder, 43 DLR (AD) 107.
